Title: Vaccinator
Education: Completion of grade 12. [ESSENTIAL], Previous EPI training, with the certificate presented and verified before contract signature. [ESSENTIAL]
Experience: One year of experience as a vaccinator in a mobile health team or in a clinic. [ESSENTIAL], Experience in emergency health projects and previous experience with international organisations are an advantage.
About Company:
Over the past few years, Afghanistan has witnessed a relative improvement in security and stability across much of the country. This has allowed humanitarian actors like INTERSOS to maintain uninterrupted access and expand services in areas that were previously hard to reach. Despite this progress, the humanitarian situation remains critical, with millions of Afghans continuing to face acute vulnerabilities due to prolonged economic hardship, natural disasters, and limited access to essential services.
In 2025, more than half of the population is in need of humanitarian assistance, with food insecurity, child malnutrition, and displacement remaining key concerns. Natural disasters, such as floods and recent earthquakes, have further compounded the needs of already struggling communities.
INTERSOS continues to operate through a community-based approach with field bases in Kabul, Kandahar, and Zabul, delivering primary healthcare, nutrition, and protection services with a focus on women, children, and persons with disabilities. The organization enjoys strong community acceptance and collaborates closely with relevant national authorities, including maintaining the full participation of female staff in all activities.
While the operational environment is largely stable and conducive, funding shortfalls and systemic barriers such as restrictions on financial flows and administrative bottlenecks continue to impact the scope and scale of humanitarian response. Sustained support is crucial to ensure the continuity of life-saving services and to address the urgent needs of Afghanistan’s most vulnerable populations.
Job Summary:
Contribute to the reduction of mortality and morbidity in the target area, in particular from vaccine-preventable diseases, by delivering routine immunisation services to children and to women of childbearing age, in accordance with the national EPI guidelines, the WHO and UNICEF protocols and the INTERSOS procedures.
The Vaccinator administers vaccines, maintains the cold chain, keeps accurate immunisation records, raises community awareness and follows up defaulters, working in the health facility and with the Mobile Health Team.
2.
Tasks and responsibilities
Delivery of immunisation services
•
Carry out the EPI activities of the project, in the fixed centre and through outreach and mobile health team activities.
•
Administer only the vaccines for which he/she has been trained and assessed as competent, and only after the competency assessment has been recorded by the EPI Officer.
•
Screen every child and every woman of childbearing age against the immunisation schedule, check the vaccination card, and administer the doses due.
•
Apply injection safety at all times: one sterile syringe and needle for each injection, no recapping, and immediate disposal in the safety box.
•
Explain to the caregiver what has been given, the possible minor reactions, and the date of the next dose, and record it on the vaccination card.
•
Never request or accept any payment for vaccination. The service is free of charge.
Cold chain and vaccine management
•
Transport and store vaccines in accordance with the EPI, UNICEF and WHO protocols.
•
Respect the cold chain principles during the transport of vaccines at all times.
•
Check the vaccine vial monitor and the expiry date before administering any dose, and discard any vaccine that does not comply, in accordance with the protocol.
•
Record the temperature of the cold chain equipment as required, and keep the record available for supervision.
•
Where a problem arises in the storage of vaccines, act immediately to transfer them to another location where a functioning cold chain is available, and inform the supervisor without delay.
•
Monitor stock levels and expiry dates, limit wastage, and alert the supervisor in advance of any risk of rupture.
Safety and adverse events
•
Recognise and manage adverse events following immunisation in accordance with the national protocol, ensure that the anaphylaxis kit is available and within its expiry date before any session begins, and keep the patient under observation as required.
•
Report every adverse event following immunisation to the EPI Officer and to the Medical Doctor without delay, and record it.
•
Apply infection prevention and control and the correct management of immunisation waste, including sharps, both in the health facility and in the mobile health team.
Community awareness, coverage and defaulter tracing
•
Raise awareness in the community and encourage caregivers to vaccinate their children and women of childbearing age.
•
Contribute to the extension of vaccination coverage in the catchment area and to the reduction of the defaulter rate.
•
Follow up the completed cases to confirm that the vaccination schedule has been completed, and identify and trace defaulting and missed children together with the Community Health Workers.
•
Participate in new EPI programmes and in public awareness campaigns.
Planning, records and reporting
•
Contribute to the preparation of an accurate working plan for the field activities of the Mobile Health Team.
•
Complete the tally sheets, registers and vaccination cards accurately and on the same day. No eligible child or woman is left unregistered, and no figure is adjusted in order to influence a reported indicator.
•
Know and work towards the annual and monthly EPI indicators of the project.
•
Report to the supervisor any problem encountered in the delivery of services, and any error or near miss occurring in the field activities of the mobile team.
Conduct and compliance
•
Treat every caregiver, child and community member with respect and without discrimination.
•
Maintain the confidentiality of the information recorded in the course of the activity.
•
Comply with the INTERSOS Charter of Values, Code of Ethics, the Policy for the Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), the Safeguarding Policy and the Anti-Fraud Policy, and report any concern through the established channels.
•
Perform any other task related to the function of the position, as assigned by the supervisor.

Job Summary:
Midwives working in Family Health Houses (FHHs) and Midwifery-Led Maternity Care Centres (MLMCCs) play a critical role in providing essential maternal, newborn and related health services to women and girls in Afghanistan. Their work can involve prolonged exposure to demanding working conditions, high workloads, emotional stress, challenging cases, and other pressures that may affect their psychosocial well-being. Recognizing the importance of staff welfare and the well-being of frontline health workers, it is critical to engage a qualified and experienced MHPSS Senior Counsellor to provide accessible, confidential, and professional psychosocial support to midwives working in selected FHHs and MLMCCs. The intervention will focus on the identified FHHs in Balkh and MLMCCs in Kabul and Logar.
Responsibilities and scope of work:
The MHPSS Senior Counsellor will be responsible for the following:
1. Psychosocial Counselling and Support
●
Conduct in-person psychosocial counselling and supportive sessions with midwives working in the targeted FHHs and MLMCCs.
●
Provide individual counselling, psychological first aid and psychosocial support based on identified needs.
●
Establish a safe, confidential, respectful and non-judgmental environment for midwives to discuss work-related stress, emotional difficulties, interpersonal concerns and other psychosocial issues.
●
Apply appropriate evidence-informed counselling and psychosocial support approaches within the counsellor's professional scope of practice.
●
Support midwives to develop healthy coping strategies, strengthen resilience and maintain their psychosocial well-being.
2. Assessment and Follow-up
●
Conduct an initial assessment of the psychosocial well-being and support needs of individual midwives.
●
Develop, jointly with each midwife, an appropriate follow-up and communication plan based on identified needs.
●
Provide follow-up counselling and psychosocial support through telephone or in-person, as appropriate.
●
Maintain regular and appropriate contact with midwives requiring continued psychosocial support.
●
Monitor progress and adjust the frequency and type of support according to individual needs.
3. Referral and Case Management
●
Identify individuals who may require specialized mental health or other professional services beyond the scope of the counselling provided.
●
Facilitate appropriate and confidential referrals to available specialized services in accordance with established referral pathways.
●
Follow up on referrals, where appropriate and with the individual's consent, while respecting confidentiality and professional boundaries.
4. Staff Welfare and Capacity Support
●
Contribute to the overall staff welfare approach for midwives working in targeted facilities.
●
Identify common psychosocial stressors and emerging staff welfare concerns affecting midwives.
●
Where appropriate, provide brief group-based psychosocial support, stress-management, or well-being sessions for midwives.
●
Provide practical recommendations on measures that may contribute to improved staff well-being and retention.
5. Coordination and Reporting
●
Coordinate closely with the supervisor and designated focal point of the implementing partner.
●
Maintain appropriate documentation of counselling and psychosocial support activities while ensuring strict confidentiality.
●
Provide regular anonymized reports on counselling activities, psychosocial needs, key challenges, referrals, and recommendations to strengthen staff welfare and support.
●
Immediately communicate any significant operational or service-delivery concerns through the appropriate reporting channels, while maintaining client confidentiality.
●
Participate in relevant coordination, review, and planning meetings as requested.
Approach and Modality:
The assignment will follow a blended model of MHPSS support, combining face-to-face and remote counselling. The MHPSS Senior Counsellor will initially visit the targeted FHHs and MLMCCs to establish contact with midwives, conduct an initial psychosocial assessment, and provide counselling/support. Following the initial visit, the counsellor will develop an individualized follow-up plan with each midwife. Subsequent support may be provided through telephone-based counselling and psychosocial check-ins, particularly for midwives working in remote locations. The frequency of follow-up will be determined according to the individual midwife's needs and the agreed communication plan. The MHPSS counsellor is expected to ensure that the modality of support is accessible, confidential, culturally appropriate, and consistent with professional ethical standards.
Reporting and Supervision:
The MHPSS Senior Counsellor will work under the overall supervision of the designated IP Project Manager.
Job Requirements:
Education
●
A Master's degree in Psychology, Counselling, Clinical Psychology, Mental Health, Social Work or another relevant field is required/preferred, depending on the applicable recruitment requirements.
Professional Experience and Technical Competencies
●
Minimum 4 years of relevant professional experience in MHPSS, psychosocial counselling, mental health, or related programming.
●
Demonstrated experience providing individual psychosocial counselling and support.
●
Experience working with health workers, frontline workers or other personnel exposed to high-stress or demanding working environments is highly desirable.
●
Experience in staff welfare, psychological first aid, stress management, resilience-building, or related interventions is an advantage.
●
Strong understanding of confidentiality, informed consent, professional boundaries and ethical counselling practice.
●
Ability to work independently, manage a caseload and organize field visits and remote follow-up effectively.
Language Requirements
●
Fluency and good communication skills in Dari and/ Pashto are mandatory.
●
Working knowledge of English is an advantage for documentation, training, and communication with programme staff.

Diagnose and manage reproductive tract infections and sexually transmitted infections.

About Company:
Over the past few years, Afghanistan has witnessed a relative improvement in security and stability across much of the country. This has allowed humanitarian actors like INTERSOS to maintain uninterrupted access and expand services in areas that were previously hard to reach. Despite this progress, the humanitarian situation remains critical, with millions of Afghans continuing to face acute vulnerabilities due to prolonged economic hardship, natural disasters, and limited access to essential services.
In 2025, more than half of the population is in need of humanitarian assistance, with food insecurity, child malnutrition, and displacement remaining key concerns. Natural disasters, such as floods and recent earthquakes, have further compounded the needs of already struggling communities.
INTERSOS continues to operate through a community-based approach with field bases in Kabul, Kandahar, and Zabul, delivering primary healthcare, nutrition, and protection services with a focus on women, children, and persons with disabilities. The organization enjoys strong community acceptance and collaborates closely with relevant national authorities, including maintaining the full participation of female staff in all activities.
While the operational environment is largely stable and conducive, funding shortfalls and systemic barriers such as restrictions on financial flows and administrative bottlenecks continue to impact the scope and scale of humanitarian response. Sustained support is crucial to ensure the continuity of life-saving services and to address the urgent needs of Afghanistan’s most vulnerable populations.

Provide nursing care, treatment and follow-up of patients according to the doctors’ prescriptions where applicable, the protocols applied in the service and the universal hygiene standards and precautions, in order to ensure the quality and continuity of care for the target population.

Perform cleaning and minor maintenance of the biomedical equipment used.

Supervise and train nurse aides, nutritional assistants, cleaners and other related staff under his/her supervision, ensuring teamwork and adherence to all the appropriate protocols and procedures.

•

Title: Regional Team Coordinator (Re Announced)
Salary: Salary and conditions are according to ACBAR’s salary scale.
Contract Duration: Contract is through 31 December, 2026, renewable on an annual basis depending on funding and performance.
Education: Bachelor’s Degree in a relevant field, including but not limited to Project Management, Humanitarian Aid, Development Policy, Business and/or Management, or another specialized field relevant to the role.  Master’s Degree is preferred.
Experience: Minimum seven (7) years of professional experience working with either NGOs or the UN in Afghanistan managing or leading humanitarian and/or development programs at the field level.
About Company:
The Agency Coordinating Body for Afghan Relief and Development (ACBAR) is an independent forum founded in 1988 in response to the demand from NGOs working with Afghan refugees in Pakistan and across the border in Afghanistan to more efficiently coordinate assistance and delivery of services. With its main office in Kabul since 2002, ACBAR brings together more than 200 National and International NGOs working in all sectors of humanitarian assistance and development in Afghanistan. Based on our three strategic pillars of Information and Coordination, Advocacy and Enabling Environment, and Capacity Building, ACBAR’s activities support our members to effectively deliver services and implement programs across Afghanistan, as well as provide services that promote ongoing organizational development and learning.   ACBAR is committed to providing
an efficient platform for members to carry out effective humanitarian, development, and peace building activities in Afghanistan.
The members are the drive behind ACBAR, and their active participation is essential to ACBAR’s continued dynamism.
With the ongoing humanitarian reset, ACBAR is taking a stronger role providing programmatic coordination for our members and implementing NGOs in numerous areas, including sub-national coordination. This year, ACBAR will serve in the secretariat role supporting newly operationalized Regional Teams (RT) in five regional hubs (Kandahar, Herat, Nangarhar, Balkh and Bamiyan).  These RTs will be responsible to support Area Based Coordination and nexus-oriented approaches in their respective regions, and responsible for coordinating BHN activities and supporting the transition from humanitarian to BHN programming where feasible and appropriate.
Job Summary:
POSITION SUMMARY
The Regional Team Coordinator (RT) supports ACBAR’s role as Secretariat to the Regional Teams (RTs), which serve as the primary sub-national coordination platform under Afghanistan’s Area-Based Coordination (ABC) and Humanitarian-Development-Peace Nexus (HDPN) framework. The RT Coordinator will ensure effective, inclusive, and well-documented coordination among Humanitarian and Basic Human Needs (BHN) actors, facilitating evidence-based planning, information sharing, and follow-up on priorities of the RT, in cooperation with two RT co-chairs per region. As part of the ACBAR team, the RT Coordinator will also engage with ACBAR’s full regional team to support the central role that ACBAR plays to strengthen NGO engagement, supporting transition from humanitarian to resilience-oriented programming, and ensuring alignment with national coordination structures.
ESSENTIAL TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES FOR THE POSITION
Secretariat and Coordination Leadership
Serve as the primary focal point for secretariat functions of the Regional Team (RT), which will be responsible to organize and coordinate monthly (and ad hoc) RT meetings, including developing priorities and agendas for meetings in consultation with RT co-chairs.
Draft and circulate meeting minutes of the RT meetings to co-chairs and all participants for further follow up on key discussions
,
decisions taken, and action points and engagement with responsible parties
Maintain updated RT membership lists and track regular participation by RT members to ensure robust engagement, facilitating inclusive participation of members, including remote/online engagement as required.
Track follow-up actions and monitor implementation of RT decisions, being the key point person to ensure that decisions taken by the RT are operationalized.
Manage integration of various other coordination platforms into the work of the RT, including the OCT (humanitarian coordination), national coordination structures (ICCT, HCT, PMT)
,
and NGO forums.
This will include actively identifying and resolving duplication, gaps or inconsistencies, and ensuring alignment with national priorities.
External Engagement and Access Support
Serve as the main focal point for external engagement on behalf of the RT, including direct engagement with provincial and local authorities, community leaders and other stakeholders required to support an enabling environment for implementing humanitarian and basic needs programs.  While leading external engagement, the RT Coordinator will engage with the co-chairs, NGOs and UN partners to successfully facilitate the engagement on behalf of the RT.
Escalate and report ongoing access and implementation challenges to the national level management of ACBAR, HAWG, and corresponding coordination mechanisms.
Strategy, Planning and Information Management
Lead the development of the RT annual action plan in cooperation with the co-chairs and members, with clear objectives and deliverables that can be tracked and monitored to demonstrate the contributions and value-add of the RT to members.
Lead information management and communication for the RT, including distribution of monthly summaries of activities to members, maintaining regular communication with co-chairs and members to carry forward RT priorities and strategies, and provide regional briefings to national coordination platforms, as needed.
Support regional-based data collection, assessments, and analysis to inform both regional and national level strategic planning, including providing support to data collection for the Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP) and the UN Strategic Framework for Afghanistan (UNSFA) and other analytic and research-oriented products and reports at the regional and national level. This will include data collection related to coordination of activities, including support for maintain an accurate 3W’s.
Support preparation of reports, updates, presentations, etc. on the ongoing work of the RT for HCT, UNCT, ACBAR Steering Committee, Donors and other interested external stakeholders.
Durable Solutions, Nexus Integration and Early Response Coordination
Support leadership of a Durable Solutions Technical Sub-Group of the RT that will support priorities of BHN programs within the region and provide support in transitioning from humanitarian to early recovery strategies.
Support coordination between the RT, ACBAR and the OCT in the event of rapid onset emergencies to streamline activities of the RT and emergency response coordination, and to ensure planning for transition from immediate response to early recovery priorities.  This will include facilitating rapid information sharing, initial situational overview, and regular coordination between all actors, in alignment with OCT coordination.
Cross-Cutting Priorities
Support strategic initiatives to promote better community engagement, accountability to affected populations (AAP), support for disability inclusion, and principled programming.
Ensure integration of key cross-cutting issues in RT coordination, including protection and centrality of protection, equality, GBV risk mitigation, PSEA reporting, and conflict sensitivity and Do No Harm principles.
Support strategic initiatives to promote Localisation, including facilitation of strong presence, participation and leadership of national and local NGOs, CSOs and WLOs within the work of the RT.
Engage with and support the ongoing work of the ACBAR Regional Office to ensure alignment with ACBAR strategic priorities and the ongoing work of the RT.
Job Requirements:
EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS:
Bachelor’s Degree in a relevant field, including but not limited to Project Management, Humanitarian Aid, Development Policy, Business and/or Management, or another specialized field relevant to the role.  Master’s Degree is preferred.
Minimum seven (7) years of professional experience working with either NGOs or the UN in Afghanistan managing or leading humanitarian and/or development programs at the field level.
Minimum three (3) years of experience supporting NGOs or UN in humanitarian coordination and representation roles.
Preference given to candidates who have worked in numerous locations in Afghanistan, including direct field work.
OTHER DESIRED SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE AND ATTRIBUTES:
Previous experience managing small-to-medium sized teams and working with many different stakeholder groups, including international organizations.
Strong analytical skills, with the ability to develop strategies and technical reports in English, Dari and/or Pashto.
Experience representing an NGO or UN agency with varied external stakeholders, including provincial and regional government officials.
Ability to manage complex coordination environments, with the ability operate under pressure and ambiguity.
Strong facilitation and negotiation skills.
The ability to work with other in a respectful and professional manner and work well as the leader of a team.

About Company:
World Vision International (WVI) began emergency relief operations in Afghanistan in 2001 by addressing the urgent needs of children and families affected by natural disasters and decades of conflict. More than a decade later, World Vision Afghanistan’s (WVA) programs have expanded to development sectors such as health, nutrition, WASH, child protection, and education, empowering women to engage in civil and social change through interfaith partnership.
WVA targets the most vulnerable in its interventions; including children, women, Internally Displace Persons (IDPs), and returnee refugees, as well as the most impoverished and marginalized families. These priorities have been chosen to contribute to our Goal of: “Improved survival and well-being of Afghan girls and boys, building the foundations for a better future for Afghan children and their communities.”
Our work is well established in Herat, Badghis, Ghor, and Faryab provinces in the western region of Afghanistan. We work closely with all levels of society including children, parents, teachers, village councils, religious leaders, ministries, provincial departments, and other national and international agencies.
Job Summary:
The WV health and nutrition programs seek to contribute to decreased morbidity and mortality in women and girls, including PLW, in the designated provinces of Afghanistan. The sector aims improve health and nutrition status of men, women, and children in particular in the marginalized and hard-to-reach areas by providing equitable, inclusive, and safe access to health and nutrition services for high-risk groups. This will encompass providing lifesaving health and nutrition services for populations in the urgent needs for health and nutrition services in the areas not covered by existing health programing in the country and engaging diverse actors to deliver integrated malnutrition treatment in communities and health facilities.
This is a full-time, grant-funded position with regular travel to the targeted district within the designated province. The primary responsibility of this role is to support the implementation of a Health and Nutrition projects at the community level, as well as to assist in planning, organizing, implementing, and monitoring the Health and Nutrition projects in the
targeted areas under direct supervision of the Zonal Manager and in close coordination with the Health and Nutrition sector lead. The individual in this role is mainly responsible for delivering project activities at the field level. Key tasks include identifying priority needs, sensitizing and mobilizing communities, establishing relationships with community leaders and local government authorities, following up on the MOU with the MoPH, delivering medical assistance, registering complaints, ensuring proper documentation, and conducting follow-ups with beneficiaries.

Since 2006, the French Medical Institute for Mothers and Children (FMIC) in Kabul, Afghanistan, has served patients from all 34 provinces. Title: Chief Surveyor
Education: B.S.c degree in civil engineering, or diploma in Surveying, Geomatics, or a related discipline.
Experience: Typically 9–12+ years of surveying experience, preferably with significant experience on major road/highway projects.
About Company:
Trust Grow Construction and Engineering Company
(TGCEC) is non-governmental, non-partisan, non- political organization and its established to assist for the development, rehabilitation and reconstruction of Afghanistan; fully controlled and run by professional, well educated, experienced and yang peoples.
TGCEC is an active construction firms working through direct cooperation with local and international communality such as Afghanistan Ministries, UN Agencies, NATO, US Army (US Army Corps of Engineering & PRT), USAID, US Embassy, NGOs and etc.
TGCEC has successfully done so many Road, Bridge, Building, survey, design, Canal, irrigation scheme and construction supervision projects in a very professional manner and on time delivery with deferent sector, National and international.
TGCEC is legally registered with Directorate General of Central Business Registry & Intellectual Property (DGCBRIP) with license number (35306) operating under Afghanistan business law framework and we do adhere great values in International business ethics.
Job Summary:
Position Summary
The Chief Surveyor is responsible for managing and supervising all surveying and setting-out activities for a road construction project. The role ensures that the road alignment, levels, coordinates, earthworks, structures, drainage, and other works are constructed accurately in accordance with approved drawings, specifications, and contractual requirements.
Job Requirements:
Job Description — Chief Surveyor, Road Project
Key Responsibilities
Manage and supervise the surveying team, including surveyors, technicians, and chainmen.
Establish and maintain project control points, benchmarks, reference stations, and survey networks.
Carry out and verify setting-out for:
Road centerline and alignment
Horizontal and vertical curves
Formation and subgrade levels
Embankments and cuttings
Pavement layers
Drainage structures and culverts
Bridges and other structures
Road furniture and ancillary works
Check coordinates, elevations, chainages, offsets, and dimensions against approved drawings.
Conduct topographical, longitudinal, and cross-sectional surveys as required.
Monitor earthwork quantities and assist with measurement and quantity calculations.
Carry out as-built surveys and prepare accurate survey records and drawings.
Review survey data and ensure accuracy before submitting it for approval.
Coordinate with the Project Manager, Construction Manager, Site Engineers, QA/QC team, and consultant's survey team.
Review construction drawings and identify discrepancies or conflicts affecting setting-out.
Ensure that surveying activities comply with project specifications, method statements, quality requirements, and applicable standards.
Operate and oversee the use of total stations, GNSS/GPS equipment, digital levels, drones where approved, and relevant surveying software.
Ensure all surveying equipment is properly maintained, calibrated, and in good working condition.
Maintain survey field books, control-point registers, calibration records, level books, calculation sheets, and other survey documentation.
Verify contractor/subcontractor survey work where applicable.
Assist the quantity surveying and commercial teams with measurement and verification of completed works.
Provide technical guidance and training to junior surveyors and survey technicians.
Identify and resolve survey-related technical issues during construction.
Ensure safe working practices are followed during all surveying activities.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree or diploma in Surveying, Geomatics, Civil Engineering, or a related discipline.
Professional surveying certification or registration is an advantage.
Strong knowledge of land surveying principles and road construction surveying.
Good knowledge of coordinate systems, benchmarks, levels, alignment, and setting-out procedures.
Proficiency with Total Station, GNSS/GPS, AutoCAD/Civil 3D, digital levels, and relevant surveying software.
Experience
Typically 9–12+ years of surveying experience, preferably with significant experience on major road/highway projects.
Previous experience in a Chief Surveyor or Senior Surveyor position is preferred.
Experience in earthworks, pavement construction, drainage, bridges, and road structures.
Experience working with consultants, contractors, and government/road authorities is an advantage.
Key Competencies
Strong technical surveying and analytical skills.
Excellent knowledge of road construction methods and tolerances.
High attention to accuracy and detail.
Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and specifications.
Strong leadership and team-management skills.
Good communication and coordination abilities.
Ability to work under pressure and meet construction deadlines.
Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills.
Commitment to quality, safety, and accurate documentation.
Reporting
The Chief Surveyor typically reports to the Project Manager / Construction Manager and coordinates closely with the Consultant/Engineer, QA/QC Manager, Site Engineers, and Quantity Surveyor.

Title: Head of Advocacy, Inclusion & Strategic Communications (Re Announced)
Salary: Salary and conditions are according to ACBAR’s salary scale.
Contract Duration: The contract is valid until 30 June 2027 and may be renewed annually, subject to funding availability and satisfactory performance.
Education: Advanced degree in humanitarian affairs, international relations, political science, communications, development studies, or a related field
Experience: Minimum 8 years of progressively responsible experience in humanitarian advocacy, NGO coordination, policy influence, or strategic engagement
About Company:
The Agency Coordinating Body for Afghan Relief and Development, ACBAR, is an independent forum founded in 1988 in response to the demand from NGOs working with Afghan refugees in Pakistan and across the border in Afghanistan to more efficiently coordinate assistance and delivery of services. With its main office in Kabul since 2002, ACBAR brings together 230 National and International NGOs working in in all sectors of humanitarian assistance and development in Afghanistan. Its activities focus heavily on information to its members and the aid community in general, coordination of activities at the national and regional levels, and advocacy on issues affecting the work of its members in Afghanistan. ACBAR has a mission
to provide an efficient platform for members to carry out effective humanitarian, development, and peace building activities in Afghanistan.
The members are the drive behind ACBAR, and their active participation is essential to ACBAR’s continued dynamism.
Job Summary:
The Head of Advocacy, Inclusion & Strategic Communications leads ACBAR’s collective NGO advocacy and strategic positioning functions in Afghanistan. The role is responsible for strengthening evidence-based advocacy, inclusive representation, strategic narrative management, and coordinated stakeholder engagement in support of ACBAR members.
The position ensures that ACBAR’s external positioning reflects principled, member-driven, and politically sensitive advocacy approaches while strengthening the participation and visibility of national NGOs, including women-led organizations and regional actors. The role also supports coherent strategic communications, messaging discipline, and reactive advocacy coordination during operational or political developments affecting NGOs.
The role contributes to strengthening linkages between national and regional coordination structures, ensuring field-level concerns and operational realities are systematically reflected in advocacy analysis, policy engagement, and donor dialogue.
Strategic Advocacy & Policy Influence
Lead the development, implementation, and periodic review of ACBAR’s advocacy strategy.
Identify emerging operational and policy issues affecting NGOs and coordinate collective advocacy responses.
Produce policy briefs, position papers, advocacy messages, briefing notes, and strategic analyses.
Support coherent NGO positioning on humanitarian principles, localization, access, taxation, civic space, and operational challenges.
Coordinate reactive advocacy efforts during emergencies, policy shifts, or incidents affecting NGO operations.
Stakeholder Engagement & Representation Support
Support leadership engagement with donors, UN agencies, de facto authorities, diplomatic missions, and other stakeholders.
Prepare strategic briefings, talking points, background notes, and engagement materials for senior leadership.
Maintain stakeholder mapping and engagement tracking systems.
Ensure all external positioning reflects agreed ACBAR and member-approved advocacy positions.
Engagement with external actors shall be conducted through designated institutional channels and agreed representation arrangements.
Inclusion & Localization
Promote inclusive participation of national NGOs, women-led NGOs, regional actors, and underrepresented groups within coordination and advocacy structures.
Provide strategic input to ensure gender-sensitive and inclusive approaches across advocacy and coordination products.
Support leadership development, advocacy capacity strengthening, and engagement readiness of national NGOs.
Coordinate exchange platforms, consultations, and learning opportunities between INGOs and NNGOs.
Strategic Communications & Narrative Management
Support development of strategic communications products aligned with ACBAR’s institutional positioning.
Contribute to messaging governance, visibility strategy, speechwriting support, and communications risk management.
Support public communication consistency across advocacy products and external engagement materials.
Coordinate with Information Sharing functions to avoid duplication and ensure coherent dissemination of information.
Regional & Member Coordination
Facilitate and coordinate the Advocacy Working Group (AWG).
Strengthen field-to-national advocacy linkages through systematic engagement with regional teams and member organizations.
Consolidate field-level feedback and operational trends into strategic analysis and advocacy messaging.
Support regional offices in addressing operational advocacy challenges.
Monitoring, Analysis & Reporting
Monitor political, humanitarian, and operational developments affecting NGOs and humanitarian action.
Produce periodic analytical updates and strategic reporting products.
Maintain awareness of evolving policy and operational risks relevant to ACBAR members.
Job Requirements:
Advanced degree in humanitarian affairs, international relations, political science, communications, development studies, or a related field.
Minimum 8 years of progressively responsible experience in humanitarian advocacy, NGO coordination, policy influence, or strategic engagement.
Strong understanding of Afghanistan’s humanitarian, political, and operational environment.
Demonstrated experience in coalition building, strategic analysis, and stakeholder engagement.
Experience working in fragile or conflict-affected settings.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English. Dari and/or Pashto desirable.
Core Competencies
Strategic thinking and political awareness
Diplomacy and stakeholder management
Advocacy and influence
Inclusive leadership and localization sensitivity
Analytical and report-writing skills
High integrity and professionalism
Ability to operate in politically sensitive environments
Performance Indicators
Quality and timeliness of advocacy products and strategic analysis
Effective facilitation of coordinated NGO messaging
Strengthened inclusion of national and regional NGO voices
Improved coherence between national and regional advocacy efforts
Quality of strategic engagement support provided to leadership
Strengthened member engagement and advocacy capacity
Additional Notes
The role is strategic and representative in nature. ACBAR advocates collectively on behalf of members and does not undertake independent political positioning outside agreed institutional frameworks.
Travel to regional offices and stakeholder meetings within Afghanistan may be required.

Job Summary:
Scope of Work:
The SRHR Mentorship Trainer is responsible for strengthening the capacity of healthcare providers through on-site mentorship, coaching, and training in Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) in compliance with the MdM and RH/MOPH standards. The position will support quality improvement initiatives, ensure adherence to national protocols and clinical guidelines, and contribute to improving access to and utilization of quality SRHR services within supported health facilities.

The SRHR Mentorship Trainer
Will be responsible for the Following SRH activités Under the direct guidance of the MdM Médical Coordinator and Project manager.
Key Responsibilities
1. Capacity Building and Mentorship
Assess the competencies, performance, and capacity-building needs of healthcare providers/staff through direct observation, review of clinical practice, and relevant assessment tools.
Develop and implement tailored mentorship and capacity-building plans based on identified competency gaps and programe priorities.
Provide practical clinical coaching on SRHR services, including family planning, ANC, PNC, safe delivery, essential newborn care, postpartum family planning, adolescent SRH, infection prevention and control, recognition of danger signs, and appropriate referral.
Conduct direct observation of clinical practice and provide practical demonstration, coaching and feedback to midwives based on identified competency gaps.
Assess training and capacity-building needs of healthcare providers.
Develop and implement mentorship plans for health staff.
Provide practical clinical coaching on SRHR service delivery, including family planning, maternal health, antenatal care (ANC), postnatal care (PNC), and adolescent reproductive health.
Support healthcare providers in applying national and international SRHR guidelines and standards.
Organize and facilitate training workshops, refresher courses, and learning sessions.
Follow up on mentorship and capacity-building activities to assess progress, identify remaining gaps, and adapt mentorship plans accordingly.
2. Quality Improvement
Monitor the quality of SRHR services through direct observation, review of clinical practices, relevant checklists and service data.
Identify gaps in service delivery and develop improvement plans.
Follow up on quality improvement actions and monitor progress and relevant quality indicators to assess improvement.
Support health facilities in implementing quality improvement measures.
Promote respectful maternity care, privacy, confidentiality, informed choice and client-centered care.
Ensure compliance with infection prevention and control standards.
Consider client/service-user feedback to identify areas for improvement in the quality and accessibility of services.
3. Technical Support
Provide technical leadership, clinical guidance, interpretation of relevant standards and guidelines, problem-solving, and technical support to healthcare facilities and programe teams on SRHR service delivery.
P
rovide technical and clinical guidance on family planning, ANC, PNC, safe delivery, essential newborn care, postpartum family planning, adolescent SRH and referral of maternal and newborn complications.
Support the integration of SRHR services into routine primary healthcare services and ensure appropriate linkages and referrals.
Promote evidence-based practices and adherence to Ministry of Public Health (MoPH) guidelines.
Support the development and updating of training materials, mentorship tools, and technical guidance as required.
4. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting
Prepare regular mentorship reports and recommendations.
Review and analyze relevant SRHR service data and indicators to identify gaps and inform mentorship priorities.
Contribute to project monitoring, evaluation, and learning activities.
Maintain accurate records of training, coaching sessions, and participant attendance.

Participate in the SRHR technical meetings and coordination forums.
Support knowledge-sharing and peer learning among healthcare providers.
Represent the project in relevant SRHR-related meetings when requested.

Adhere to MdM safeguarding, PSEA, and other relevant organizational policies and procedures.

Promote confidentiality, dignity, privacy, informed choice, and respectful treatment of all beneficiaries/service-users.
·
Promote safe and confidential reporting and referral of safeguarding, PSEA, protection, and other concerns in line with MdM procedures.
Ensure accountability to affected populations and communities.

About Company:
PARSA’s mission is to train and develop Afghan leaders who support Afghan communities and civil society by providing and facilitating innovative and impactful programs. Job Summary:
The Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) Assistant is a full-time position that is responsible to support the Deputy Program Manager
-HAF
in monitoring, evaluation, accountability, learning, documentation, and quality assurance for the Healthy Afghan Family (HAF) Program and related Safe Space (SS) activities under PARSA.
The position supports data collection, verification, analysis, reporting, field monitoring, case management tracking, database management, Kobo surveys, beneficiary assessments, post-implementation monitoring, and documentation of success stories, case studies, and lessons learned.
The MEAL Assistant works closely with case workers, facilitators, interns, volunteers, and project staff to ensure program information is accurate, timely, complete, confidential, and properly documented.
The position also supports monitoring of beneficiary participation and progress, economic empowerment activities, staff capacity-building activities, and follow-up actions arising from monitoring findings as well as provides timely information to the Deputy Program Manager to support program learning, quality improvement, and informed decision-making.

About Company:
Medair is an international humanitarian organization established in 1988. Medair has been operating in Afghanistan since 1996 with programs mainly in the Health, Water & Sanitation, and Livelihoods sectors with significant reconstruction activities in remote areas. Current projects are Water & Sanitation, Food Security, & Disaster Risk Reduction.
An Integrated Emergency Response: Medair aims to respond to high levels of food insecurity, malnutrition, and morbidity in Tirinkot district.  The project intends to improve and extend WASH services including water supply infrastructure and hygiene practices to improve outcomes for vulnerable families.
An Integrated Emergency Response:
Medair aims to respond to high levels of food insecurity, malnutrition, and morbidity in Uruzgan, which has been significantly affected by drought and conflict conditions. Building upon Medair’s decades of experience in the Central Highlands and Kandahar, the project intends to improve and extend the utilization of lifesaving preventive and curative nutrition and health services by mothers, PLWs, and children U5; to increase access to clean water, to reduce vulnerability to water-related and other preventable diseases, and to improve and increase food security for the most vulnerable families through food voucher distributions.
Job Summary:
Overall purpose
To serve as a member of the Basic Health Centre (BHC) team by providing high-quality routine immunization services at outreach sites and within communities across the catchment area. The Vaccinator is responsible for conducting vaccination sessions in accordance with national EPI guidelines, identifying and tracing zero-dose, under-immunized, and dropout children, maintaining vaccine cold chain and reporting systems, and promoting community awareness and acceptance of immunization services. Working closely with female vaccinators, CHNVs, community leaders, and health facility staff, the role contributes to increasing routine immunization coverage, reducing vaccine dropout rates, strengthening disease prevention efforts, and supporting integrated primary health care services through outreach activities.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Provide routine immunization services at outreach sites and within communities in accordance with National EPI guidelines, Medair protocols, and established vaccination schedules.
Plan and conduct outreach vaccination sessions in villages/mosques and hard-to-reach areas, ensuring eligible children and pregnant women have access to immunization services.
Identify, trace, and follow up zero-dose, under-immunized, and dropout children through household visits, review of EPI records, and coordination with community structures.
Ensure proper vaccine stock management, cold chain maintenance, temperature monitoring, safe injection practices, and appropriate disposal of medical waste according to EPI standards.
Coordinate with Community Health Nutrition Volunteers (CHNVs), Community Health Supervisors (CHSs), community leaders, religious leaders, and Health Shuras to promote immunization uptake and reduce vaccine hesitancy.
Maintain accurate vaccination records, tally sheets, registers, and reporting tools, and submit timely daily and monthly reports to the Health Facility Supervisor.
Monitor and report missed children, vaccine refusals, migration-related defaulters, vaccine wastage, and other challenges affecting immunization coverage, providing recommendations for improvement.
Support integrated outreach activities alongside nutrition, maternal, newborn, and child health services, including referral of children and pregnant women requiring additional health services.
Participate in supplementary immunization activities, polio campaigns, outbreak response activities, and other public health interventions as assigned by the line manager.
Ensure all outreach activities are implemented in accordance with national guidelines, organizational protocols, accountability standards, and infection prevention and control measures.
Undertake any other duties relevant to the role as assigned by the Line Manager
MAIN ACTIVITIES
Outreach Vaccination Responsibilities:
Conduct routine immunization and vaccination activities at outreach sites and within communities in accordance with National EPI guidelines.
Plan and implement outreach vaccination sessions according to the approved micro-plan and schedule.
Identify, register, trace, and follow up zero-dose, under-immunized, and dropout children to ensure completion of the vaccination schedule.
Conduct household visits and community mapping to identify eligible children under one year of age and pregnant women requiring immunization services.
Participate in Polio campaigns, supplementary immunization activities, outbreak response interventions, and other national immunization initiatives as assigned by the LM.
Provide health education and counselling to caregivers and community members on the importance of immunization, vaccine schedules, and vaccine-preventable diseases.
·

About Première Urgence - Aide Médicale Internationale (PU-AMI)
PU-AMI (known globally as Première Urgence Internationale, PUI) is a non-governmental, non-profit, non-political and non-religious international aid organization. PU-AMI’s teams are committed to support vulnerable communities and populations, those marginalized, hit by conflict, natural disaster or economic downturns. PU-AMI’s main objective is to contribute to reduction in morbidity and mortality, and provide emergency relief to those in immediate need in order to help them regain their dignity.
Afghan mission is the oldest of PUI missions, with the first medical intervention launched in 1979 just after the Soviet troops crossed the country’s borders. PU-AMI teams currently deliver the integrated health care, combined with nutrition, psychosocial support; water, sanitation and hygiene (wash), as well as trauma services. The organization implements projects mainly in eastern parts of the country, and increasingly in the South-East Region. Since the COVID-19 outbreak in 2020, PU-AMI has also positioned itself as one of the main actors in preparedness and response to the pandemic, implementing health and wash-cantered activities at health facilities and community level in Kabul and beyond.
Globally, PUI provides assistance to around 6 million people in 23 countries and across 5 continents: Africa, Asia, Middle East, Latin America, and Europe.

Overall Objective
The Guard/Cleaner is responsible for maintaining a safe, secure, clean, and hygienic environment at the SHC in accordance with MoPH Afghanistan, BPHS/EPHS guidelines, IPC standards, and organizational policies.
The position provides basic security, access control, cleaning, sanitation, healthcare waste segregation and disposal, and general facility support, while protecting patients, staff, medicines, equipment, and facility assets. The Guard/Cleaner must maintain professional, respectful, non-discriminatory, and confidential conduct and promptly report any security, safety, hygiene, or maintenance concerns to the supervisor.
Key Responsibilities
Facility Security and Access Control
·
Maintain security of the SHC premises, staff, patients, equipment, medicines, and other assets.
·
Monitor and control access to the health facility and restrict unauthorized entry.
·
Maintain orderly movement of patients and visitors within the facility.
·
Immediately report security incidents, threats, suspicious activities, or safety concerns to the supervisor.
Cleaning and Hygiene
·
Maintain cleanliness of consultation rooms, waiting areas, toilets, corridors, compound, and other facility areas.
·
Conduct regular cleaning and disinfection of high-touch surfaces and designated areas.
·
Ensure cleaning activities are performed according to facility hygiene and IPC procedures.
·
Keep the facility environment clean, safe, and welcoming for patients and staff.
Healthcare Waste Management
·
Collect, segregate, and dispose of healthcare waste according to established waste-management procedures.
·
Ensure proper separation of general, infectious, and sharps waste in designated containers.
·
Never handle or dispose of sharps or hazardous waste improperly.
·
Report damaged, overflowing, or incorrectly used waste containers to the responsible staff.
Infection Prevention and Control (IPC)
·
Follow basic IPC measures while performing cleaning and waste-management duties.
·
Use appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) during cleaning and waste handling.
·
Maintain proper hand hygiene and safe cleaning practices.
·
Immediately report spills, contamination, or other IPC risks to the supervisor.
Facility and Compound Maintenance
·
Keep the facility compound, entrances, pathways, and surrounding areas clean and free from hazards.
·
Support basic facility arrangements, including cleaning and preparation of rooms and service areas.
·
Report damaged doors, windows, locks, water systems, electrical systems, furniture, or other infrastructure concerns.
·
Support prevention of environmental hazards such as standing water, waste accumulation, and blocked drainage.
Patient Safety and Support
·
Maintain a safe and organized environment for patients, caregivers, and staff.
·
Support orderly patient flow without interfering with clinical decisions or patient confidentiality.
·
Provide respectful and non-discriminatory assistance to patients and visitors when required.
·
Give priority assistance to vulnerable patients when appropriate, while referring clinical needs to health staff.

About Company:

Job Summary:
The construction/site Engineer is responsible for supervising all the construction activities in the project sites including technical supervision, coordination, and monitoring of all the construction activities assigned as per the project technical documents and BoQ. Incumbent shall ensure all works are in accordance with the approved engineering drawings, technical specifications, contract requirements, applicable building codes, and the organization policies.
The incumbent is also responsible for quality control and quality assurance of the construction materials against the agreed standards in the project technical documents and ensuring smooth implementation as per the project timeline. He is also responsible for provision of technical advice to the contractor during construction work and project implementation. Under the overall supervision and guidance of the project manager/management the construction/site engineer undertakes the following duties.
Key Duties and Responsibilities
Technical Duties
Supervise and monitor all daily construction activities carried out by the contractor.
Ensure all construction works are executed in accordance with approved engineering drawings, technical specifications, method statements, and project schedules.
Coordinate daily work activities with the project manager and management as required.
Monitor manpower, construction equipment, and material resources to ensure efficient project execution.
Ensure work is performed safely, efficiently, and in compliance with project quality requirements.
Provide technical guidance to contractors and construction personnel on site.
Resolve routine technical issues encountered during construction.
Measure and verify completed construction quantities for progress monitoring and contractor payment purposes.
Review quantity calculations against approved Bills of Quantities (BOQ).
Assist in preparing measurement sheets and quantity reconciliation reports.
Monitor material consumption and identify excessive wastage.
Verify site setting-out, benchmarks, grid lines, elevations, and dimensions before commencement of construction.
Check dimensions, verticality, and levels of completed works before approval.
Monitor safe working practices throughout the construction site.
Ensure workers use the required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).
Report unsafe conditions, unsafe acts, accidents, and near-miss incidents.
Promote good housekeeping and environmental protection throughout the project.
Material Inspection and Control
Inspect construction materials upon delivery to ensure compliance with approved specifications.
Ensure only approved materials are used in construction.
Verify that all materials conform to approved technical specifications and project requirements.
Review manufacturers' certificates, test certificates, and material approval documents.
Review laboratory test reports and verify compliance with project specifications.
Conduct site inspections before approving work for subsequent construction activities.
Monitor proper storage, handling, and protection of materials on site.
Coordinate material inspections with project officer and procurement team.
Report damaged, defective, or non-compliant materials for corrective action.
Technical Documentation
Maintain accurate records of daily site activities, inspections, measurements, and construction progress.
Prepare daily site diaries, work progress reports, and technical reports.
Record site instructions, requests for information (RFIs), and engineering clarifications.
Review and maintain approved construction drawings, specifications, and method statements.
Ensure all technical documentation is maintained in accordance with standard document control procedures.
Contractor Coordination
Coordinate daily construction activities with contractor and management.
Conduct site coordination meetings to review progress, work priorities, and technical issues.
Ensure contractor has sufficient manpower, equipment, and materials to meet project schedules.
Monitor contractor compliance with contract requirements and approved work programs.
Assist in resolving technical disputes and construction-related issues.

Knowledge and experience of MS office and other engineering statistical programs such as AutoCAD, and other related construction design programs
Full knowledge of designing and implementation of Construction works.

Experience with field level coordination with national/international organizations.

Excellent communication, cooperation, and interpersonal skills.

Ability to organize, plan and prioritize multiple tasks and meet deadlines.
Ability to coach and inspire.
Be excellent team player.
Good coordination skills
Excellent Communication skills.
Problem solving skills in day to day and crisis situations.
Readiness to work out of office hours.
Cultural sensitivity and experience in crisis management on different level
Fluency in Dari / Pashto and English

About Company:
World Vision International (WVI) began emergency relief operations in Afghanistan in 2001 by addressing the urgent needs of children and families affected by natural disasters and decades of conflict. More than a decade later, World Vision Afghanistan’s (WVA) programs have expanded to development sectors such as health, nutrition, WASH, child protection, and education, empowering women to engage in civil and social change through interfaith partnership.
WVA targets the most vulnerable in its interventions; including children, women, Internally Displace Persons (IDPs), and returnee refugees, as well as the most impoverished and marginalized families. These priorities have been chosen to contribute to our Goal of: “Improved survival and well-being of Afghan girls and boys, building the foundations for a better future for Afghan children and their communities.”
Our work is well established in Herat, Badghis, Ghor, and Faryab provinces in the western region of Afghanistan. We work closely with all levels of society including children, parents, teachers, village councils, religious leaders, ministries, provincial departments, and other national and international agencies.
Job Summary:
Job Summary
Job Purpose
The FSAC NGO Co-chair strengthens effective, inclusive, transparent, and accountable NGO engagement and representation within the Afghanistan Food Security and Agriculture Cluster (FSAC).
Hosted by World Vision Afghanistan and functionally guided by the National FSAC Cluster Coordinator, the position facilitates systematic consultation and information exchange with national and international NGOs, NGO coordination mechanisms, and Regional NGO Co-Chairs. The role consolidates and represents collective NGO priorities, operational concerns, and agreed positions; strengthens NGO participation in FSAC processes; and ensures effective linkages between national and sub-national coordination structures.
The position co-chairs National FSAC coordination meetings and contributes to key FSAC processes, including the Seasonal Food Security Assessment (SFSA), IPC Acute Food Insecurity (AFI) Analysis, joint assessments and sectoral needs analysis, contingency and preparedness planning, seasonal prioritization, FSAC strategy development, partner information management, collective advocacy, and resource mobilization. The role ensures that NGO perspectives, regional priorities, field evidence, operational constraints, and programme information systematically inform FSAC analysis, planning, advocacy, and decision-making.
The position promotes strong coordination and constructive engagement with FSAC partners, UN agencies, humanitarian coordination mechanisms, relevant authorities, civil society, and other stakeholders while contributing to the overall effectiveness, accountability, and transparency of FSAC coordination.
When performing the FSAC NGO Co-Chair function, the position holder represents the collective and agreed interests of the NGO constituency and is expected to maintain impartiality between this representative function and their responsibilities as a World Vision Afghanistan employee.
The position reports administratively to the WVA Programme Development & Quality Director and works closely with the FSL Sector Lead for sector-specific technical guidance and alignment. The National FSAC Coordinator provides functional guidance and follows up on delivery of the FSAC NGO Co-Chair responsibilities.
Major Responsibilities
1.
NGO Coordination, Consultation & Representation Responsibilities
Establish and maintain regular information exchange and consultation with national and international NGOs, NGO coordination mechanisms, and FSAC members.
Establish a structured NGO constituency consultation mechanism to regularly identify, document and validate collective NGO priorities, concerns and positions for representation within FSAC, including differing views where consensus is not reached.
Maintain strong links with Regional NGO Co-Chairs to understand regional priorities, operational constraints, response gaps, and emerging concerns.
Represent the collective interests, priorities, concerns, and agreed positions of the NGO community during National FSAC meetings and other authorized humanitarian coordination forums.
Ensure NGO representation is impartial, transparent, consultative, and based on constituency inputs rather than the interests of the hosting organization.
Facilitate effective two-way communication between national FSAC structures and regional/sub-national NGO members.
Mobilize NGOs to address gaps in Regional NGO Co-Chair arrangements where required.
Encourage strong and diverse NGO participation in FSAC meetings, working groups, trainings, workshops, assessments, and other coordination processes.
Proactively strengthen the meaningful participation and representation of national NGOs in FSAC coordination, assessments, technical processes, strategic planning and decision-making, including identifying and addressing barriers to their participation.
Ensure NGO representation is impartial, transparent, consultative, and based on agreed constituency positions rather than the institutional interests of the hosting organization.
2.
FSAC Coordination, Co-Chairing, Accountability & Transparency
Responsibilities
Co-chair National FSAC coordination meetings in collaboration with the FSAC Coordinator and relevant Co-Leads/Co-Chairs.
Support preparation of meeting agendas, strategic discussion points, action tracking, and follow-up.
Promote accountability and transparency in FSAC decision-making, coordination processes, and agreed actions.
Follow up with NGO members on commitments and actions agreed through FSAC coordination mechanisms.
Encourage FSAC members to regularly report achievements, operational coverage, response gaps, and implementation constraints through established FSAC reporting mechanisms.
Strengthening communication and information flow between the FSAC Coordination Team and NGO membership.
Contribute to strengthening the overall effectiveness of national and sub-national FSAC coordination.
3.
Humanitarian Analysis, Assessments, Information Management & Strategic Planning Responsibilities
Contributes to the development, implementation, analysis, and dissemination of the Seasonal Food Security Assessment (SFSA).
Support NGO participation in the IPC Acute Food Insecurity (AFI) Analysis.
Facilitate coordination of joint food security and agriculture assessments and sectoral needs analysis.
Mobilize NGOs for assessment planning, data collection, validation, analysis, and dissemination exercises.
Coordinate the collection, consolidation, review, and analysis of partner information on food security and agriculture activities.
Support identification of operational coverage, duplication, geographic gaps, underserved populations, and emerging food security concerns.
Contribute to contingency planning, preparedness, strategic response planning, and seasonal prioritization.
Contribute to the development and implementation of the FSAC Strategy and Plan for 2027/28.
Promote evidence-based decision-making by ensuring field realities and NGO operational evidence inform FSAC analysis and strategic planning.
4
. Policy, Strategy, Advocacy & Resource Mobilization
Responsibilities
Contribute to FSAC policies, strategies, work plans, technical products, advocacy briefs, newsletters, and other coordination documents on behalf of the NGO community.
Consult NGO members to identify common advocacy priorities and consolidate collective positions.
Support collective advocacy on humanitarian priorities, food insecurity, operational constraints, humanitarian access, and response gaps.
Support advocacy related to funding gaps and resource mobilization in coordination with the FSAC Coordination Team.
Ensure advocacy messages and positions are evidence-based and reflect agreed NGO/FSAC priorities.
Support communication of key FSAC priorities to relevant humanitarian stakeholders.
5.
External Coordination, Partnerships & Humanitarian Representation Responsibilities
Represent FSAC, as delegated and in coordination with the FSAC Coordination Team, in relevant humanitarian forums, including ICCT, working groups, contingency planning, preparedness meetings, and other inter-cluster mechanisms.
Maintain appropriate dialogue with national and local authorities, relevant state institutions, and local civil society where feasible and in accordance with applicable HCT policies and humanitarian principles.
Build constructive relationships with NGOs, UN agencies, donors, humanitarian actors, civil society organizations, and other stakeholders relevant to FSAC objectives.
Ensure relevant information and decisions from external coordination forums are communicated back to the FSAC Coordination Team and NGO constituency.
6.
Field Engagement & Regional Coordination Responsibilities
Conduct regular field missions to regions, provinces, and districts, with a minimum of three field missions per year.
Engage Regional NGO Co-Chairs, FSAC partners, communities, and relevant stakeholders to understand food security conditions, programme gaps, access constraints, and operational challenges.
Support Regional NGO Co-Chairs and regional coordination structures where capacity or representation gaps are identified.
Document field findings and ensure relevant regional and operational issues are elevated to National FSAC discussions.
7.
Reporting, Documentation, Compliance & Other Coordination Support Responsibilities
Maintain appropriate records of NGO consultations, agreed positions, decisions, commitments, and follow-up actions.
Provide regular updates on activities, achievements, challenges, and emerging priorities to the FSL Sector Lead and FSAC Coordinator.
Manage sensitive information appropriately and maintain confidentiality.
Identify and disclose actual or perceived conflicts of interest and support their appropriate management.
Comply with World Vision safeguarding, PSEA, Code of Conduct, security, and other organizational requirements.
Undertake other relevant coordination responsibilities assigned by the FSAC Coordinator within the purpose and scope of the position.
8.
Adhere to WV accountability standards.
Adhere to WV Child and Adult Safeguarding policy and standards.
Adhere to WV accountability standards.
To be aware and prepared to implement WV Afghanistan Humanitarian and Emergency Affairs plan

Draft and maintain procedure manuals for all accounting and reporting functions and enhance the implementation of financial and accounting systems, processes, tools and control systems.
Supervise staff of Finance Department and develop/train/motivate the team as appropriate.
Meet regularly with employees of Finance Dept to review work in progress, discuss and resolve administrative, workload and technical issues.
Generate accurate monthly financial reports, including income statements, cash flow statements, and balance sheets using QuickBooks.
Manage staff through proper delegation and work supervision to provide appropriate levels of service and resources.
Other job-related duties as assigned by the Senior Management.

Master degree in Finance & Accounting field.
Professional certification e.g. ACCA, CIA, CBA, CPA, CISA or CFE will be an advantage.
At least 5 years related experience in Finance/Accounting where 2-3 years on managerial position.
Strong interpersonal skills, ability to communicate and manage well at all levels of the organization.
Knowledge of Afghan financial sector’s legal and regulatory framework.
QuickBooks Pro Advisor certification
Experience in payroll processing and tax filing within QuickBooks
Familiarity with integrating QuickBooks with other related software
Strong problem solving and creative skills and the ability to exercise sound judgment and make decision based on accurate and timely analysis.

About Company:
Human Medical Laboratories was established in 2015 under the brand Name HUMAN LABS
®
in Kabul, Afghanistan. HUMAN LABS
®
is engaged in providing various kinds of Genotyping, PCR/ Molecular Biology, Histopathology, immunohistochemistry, Microbiology, Hematopathology, Chemical Pathology, and Routine laboratory testing services. These tests are performed on state-of-the-art technology by qualified pathologists, laboratory scientists, and technologists. Our trained, effective customer service personnel also provide home sampling Collection services for ease and maximum access. The employee has been engaged and has had a great deal of experience in the designated position and subject area of his expertise.
Job Summary:
Job Summary
The Histotechnologist is responsible for performing and assisting with laboratory procedures related to histopathology, cytology, immunohistochemistry (IHC), and hematology. The position ensures accurate specimen processing, slide preparation, staining, quality control, equipment maintenance, and proper documentation while following laboratory safety procedures and professional standards.
Key Responsibilities
1. Histopathology
Receive, identify, accession, and properly handle tissue specimens.
Perform tissue fixation, processing, dehydration, clearing, and paraffin embedding.
Cut tissue sections using a microtome and prepare high-quality slides.
Perform routine H&E staining and special stains as required.
Assist with frozen-section procedures when applicable.
Maintain proper specimen identification and traceability.
Assist pathologists by preparing slides and ensuring specimens are ready for microscopic examination.
2. Cytology
Receive and process cytology specimens, including Pap smears, body fluids, FNAC samples, and other cytological specimens.
Prepare direct smears, cytospin preparations, and cell blocks when required.
Perform appropriate cytological staining procedures.
Maintain specimen integrity and accurate identification.
Assist in screening and preparation of cytology slides according to laboratory policy and applicable regulations.
3. Immunohistochemistry (IHC)
Perform tissue preparation and immunohistochemical staining according to established protocols.
Prepare and run appropriate positive and negative controls.
Handle antibodies, reagents, and detection systems correctly.
Perform troubleshooting of staining problems and report abnormal results or technical issues to the supervisor/pathologist.
Maintain IHC reagent inventory and monitor expiration dates.
Ensure proper documentation and quality control of IHC procedures.
4. Hematology
Perform routine hematology investigations, including CBC, peripheral blood smear preparation and staining.
Prepare and examine peripheral blood smears as required.
Recognize abnormal cell morphology and refer suspicious findings to the responsible department head.
Operate and maintain hematology analyzers according to manufacturer instructions.
Perform internal quality control and troubleshoot instrument problems.
5. Quality Control & Laboratory Management
Follow laboratory SOPs, quality assurance, and quality control procedures.
Participate in internal and external quality assessment programs when applicable.
Maintain accurate records of specimens, tests, controls, reagents, and equipment.
Monitor reagent quality, storage conditions, and expiration dates.
Perform routine maintenance and cleaning of laboratory equipment.
Identify and report non-conformities, specimen problems, and equipment malfunctions.
Maintain confidentiality of patient information and laboratory results.
6. Safety & Infection Control
Follow laboratory biosafety and infection-control procedures.
Properly use PPE and handle biological specimens safely.
Dispose of sharps, chemicals, and biological waste according to laboratory policies.
Follow procedures for spills, exposure incidents, and other laboratory emergencies.

Title: Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) Officer
Contract Duration: One year, with a three-month probationary period, renewable based on satisfactory performance and organizational needs.
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Monitoring and Evaluation, Statistics, Economics, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Project Management, Information Management, or another relevant field. A master’s degree in a relevant field is an advantage.
Experience: Minimum 3 years of relevant professional experience in monitoring and evaluation, project monitoring, research, data management, or results-based reporting, preferably with an NGO, civil society organization, or donor-funded project.
About Company: Begum Organization for Women (BOW) is an Afghan organization working to improve access to education, health information and health services, psychosocial support, reliable information, and public awareness through media and community-focused programs.
Job Summary:
The Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Officer will support Begum Organization for Women (BOW) in monitoring the implementation, progress, quality, and results of its projects and programs.
The M&E Officer will work closely with project managers and program teams to track activities against approved work plans, indicators, and targets. The position will also be responsible for collecting and verifying data, maintaining project evidence and databases, supporting donor reporting, and identifying gaps that require follow-up.
The M&E Officer will support monitoring across BOW’s different areas of work, including education, health, media and radio programming, digital learning, training and capacity building, climate awareness, social cohesion.
Main responsibilities include:
Develop and maintain M&E plans, indicator trackers, monitoring tools, databases, and project dashboards.
Regularly monitor project activities, outputs, indicators, and targets against approved work plans.
Collect, verify, organize, and analyze quantitative and qualitative project data.
Plan, develop, and conduct baseline and endline surveys to measure changes in project indicators and assess project results and impact.
Analyze and compare baseline and endline data and prepare clear findings and recommendations for project teams, management, and donor reporting.
Ensure that reported results have proper supporting evidence, such as participant lists, attendance sheets, broadcast logs, recordings, screenshots, links, pre- and post-tests, survey data, and partner reports.
Monitor radio programs, multimedia, digital, training, and other project activities, as required.
Develop and use surveys, questionnaires, feedback forms, interview guides, monitoring checklists, baseline and endline tools, and other M&E tools.
Collect and analyze feedback from participants and audiences through surveys, interviews, calls, WhatsApp, social media, and other appropriate channels.
Support the preparation of case studies, success stories, and stories of change.
Prepare regular M&E updates and provide accurate data and analysis for internal and donor reports.
Support project assessments, baseline and endline studies, monitoring visits, evaluations, and impact studies.
Maintain complete and well-organized project documentation and means of verification for donor monitoring, evaluations, and audits.
